audit_status.source_base: Greek Gospel text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for feeding four thousand, sign demand, leaven warning, loaves misunderstanding, Bethsaida two-stage sight, Peter confession, first passion prediction, Peter rebuke, cross-following, psyche language.

verses.restored: In those days, when again there was a great crowd and they had nothing to eat, he called the disciples and said to them,

familiar.text: In those days the multitude being very great, and having nothing to eat, Jesus called his disciples unto him, and saith unto them,

modern.text: In those days the crowd once again became very large, and they had nothing to eat. Jesus called the disciples to Him and said,

original.text: Ἐν ἐκείναις ταῖς ἡμέραις ⸂πάλιν πολλοῦ⸃ ὄχλου ὄντος καὶ μὴ ἐχόντων τί φάγωσιν, ⸀προσκαλεσάμενος τοὺς ⸀μαθητὰς λέγει αὐτοῖς·

verses.restored: I am moved with compassion for the crowd, because they remain with me three days and have nothing to eat.

familiar.text: I have compassion on the multitude, because they have now been with me three days, and have nothing to eat:

modern.text: “I have compassion for this crowd, because they have already been with Me three days and have nothing to eat.

original.text: Σπλαγχνίζομαι ἐπὶ τὸν ὄχλον ὅτι ἤδη ἡμέραι τρεῖς προσμένουσίν μοι καὶ οὐκ ἔχουσιν τί φάγωσιν·

verses.restored: If I release them hungry to their houses, they will faint on the way; and some of them have come from far away.

familiar.text: And if I send them away fasting to their own houses, they will faint by the way: for divers of them came from far.

modern.text: If I send them home hungry, they will faint along the way. For some of them have come a great distance.”

original.text: καὶ ἐὰν ἀπολύσω αὐτοὺς νήστεις εἰς οἶκον αὐτῶν, ἐκλυθήσονται ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ· ⸂καί τινες⸃ αὐτῶν ⸀ἀπὸ μακρόθεν ⸀ἥκασιν.

verses.restored: His disciples answered, From where will anyone be able to feed these people with bread here in a deserted place?

familiar.text: And his disciples answered him, From whence can a man satisfy these men with bread here in the wilderness?

modern.text: His disciples replied, “Where in this desolate place could anyone find enough bread to feed all these people?”

original.text: καὶ ἀπεκρίθησαν αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ⸀ὅτι Πόθεν τούτους δυνήσεταί τις ὧδε χορτάσαι ἄρτων ἐπʼ ἐρημίας;

verses.restored: He asked them, How many loaves do you have? They said, Seven.

familiar.text: And he asked them, How many loaves have ye? And they said, Seven.

modern.text: “How many loaves do you have?” Jesus asked. “Seven,” they replied.

original.text: καὶ ⸀ἠρώτα αὐτούς· Πόσους ἔχετε ἄρτους; οἱ δὲ εἶπαν· Ἑπτά.

verses.restored: He instructed the crowd to recline on the ground; taking the seven loaves, giving thanks, he broke them and gave them to his disciples to set before them; and they set them before the crowd.

familiar.text: And he commanded the people to sit down on the ground: and he took the seven loaves, and gave thanks, and brake, and gave to his disciples to set before them; and they did set them before the people.

modern.text: And He instructed the crowd to sit down on the ground. Then He took the seven loaves, gave thanks and broke them, and gave them to His disciples to set before the people. And they distributed them to the crowd.

original.text: καὶ ⸀παραγγέλλει τῷ ὄχλῳ ἀναπεσεῖν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς· καὶ λαβὼν τοὺς ἑπτὰ ἄρτους εὐχαριστήσας ἔκλασεν καὶ ἐδίδου τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ ἵνα ⸀παρατιθῶσιν καὶ παρέθηκαν τῷ ὄχλῳ.

verses.restored: They also had a few little fish; blessing them, he said to set these before them also.

familiar.text: And they had a few small fishes: and he blessed, and commanded to set them also before them.

modern.text: They also had a few small fish, and Jesus blessed them and ordered that these be set before them as well.

original.text: καὶ εἶχον ἰχθύδια ὀλίγα· καὶ εὐλογήσας ⸀αὐτὰ εἶπεν ⸂καὶ ταῦτα παρατιθέναι⸃.

verses.restored: They ate and were filled, and they took up seven baskets of broken pieces remaining.

familiar.text: So they did eat, and were filled: and they took up of the broken meat that was left seven baskets.

modern.text: The people ate and were satisfied, and the disciples picked up seven basketfuls of broken pieces that were left over.

original.text: ⸂καὶ ἔφαγον⸃ καὶ ἐχορτάσθησαν, καὶ ἦραν περισσεύματα κλασμάτων ἑπτὰ σπυρίδας.

verses.restored: There were about four thousand. He released them.

familiar.text: And they that had eaten were about four thousand: and he sent them away.

modern.text: And about four thousand men were present. As soon as Jesus had dismissed the crowd,

original.text: ἦσαν ⸀δὲ ὡς τετρακισχίλιοι. καὶ ἀπέλυσεν αὐτούς.

verses.restored: Immediately, entering the boat with his disciples, he came into the region of Dalmanutha.

familiar.text: And straightway he entered into a ship with his disciples, and came into the parts of Dalmanutha.

modern.text: He got into the boat with His disciples and went to the district of Dalmanutha. The Demand for a Sign (Matthew 16:1–4; Luke 12:54–56)

original.text: καὶ ⸀εὐθὺς ἐμβὰς εἰς τὸ πλοῖον μετὰ τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ ἦλθεν εἰς τὰ μέρη Δαλμανουθά.

verses.restored: The Pharisees came out and began to argue with him, seeking from him a sign from heaven, testing him.

familiar.text: And the Pharisees came forth, and began to question with him, seeking of him a sign from heaven, tempting him.

modern.text: Then the Pharisees came and began to argue with Jesus, testing Him by demanding from Him a sign from heaven.

original.text: Καὶ ἐξῆλθον οἱ Φαρισαῖοι καὶ ἤρξαντο συζητεῖν αὐτῷ, ζητοῦντες παρʼ αὐτοῦ σημεῖον ἀπὸ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, πειράζοντες αὐτόν.

verses.restored: Sighing deeply in his spirit, he said, Why does this generation seek a sign? Amen, I say to you: no sign will be given to this generation.

familiar.text: And he sighed deeply in his spirit, and saith, Why doth this generation seek after a sign? verily I say unto you, There shall no sign be given unto this generation.

modern.text: Jesus sighed deeply in His spirit and said, “Why does this generation demand a sign? Truly I tell you, no sign will be given to this generation.”

original.text: καὶ ἀναστενάξας τῷ πνεύματι αὐτοῦ λέγει· Τί ἡ γενεὰ αὕτη ⸂ζητεῖ σημεῖον⸃; ἀμὴν λέγω ⸀ὑμῖν, εἰ δοθήσεται τῇ γενεᾷ ταύτῃ σημεῖον.

verses.restored: Leaving them, he again entered the boat and went away to the other side.

familiar.text: And he left them, and entering into the ship again departed to the other side.

modern.text: And He left them, got back into the boat, and crossed to the other side. The Leaven of the Pharisees and of Herod (Matthew 16:5–12; Luke 12:1–3)

original.text: καὶ ἀφεὶς αὐτοὺς ⸂πάλιν ἐμβὰς⸃ ἀπῆλθεν εἰς τὸ πέραν.

verses.restored: They forgot to take bread, and except for one loaf they had none with them in the boat.

familiar.text: Now the disciples had forgotten to take bread, neither had they in the ship with them more than one loaf.

modern.text: Now the disciples had forgotten to take bread, except for one loaf they had with them in the boat.

original.text: Καὶ ἐπελάθοντο λαβεῖν ἄρτους, καὶ εἰ μὴ ἕνα ἄρτον οὐκ εἶχον μεθʼ ἑαυτῶν ἐν τῷ πλοίῳ.

verses.restored: He instructed them, saying, Watch; beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and the leaven of Herod.

familiar.text: And he charged them, saying, Take heed, beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, and of the leaven of Herod.

modern.text: “Watch out!” He cautioned them. “Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and of Herod.”

original.text: καὶ διεστέλλετο αὐτοῖς λέγων· Ὁρᾶτε, βλέπετε ἀπὸ τῆς ζύμης τῶν Φαρισαίων καὶ τῆς ζύμης Ἡρῴδου.

verses.restored: They were reasoning with one another because they had no bread.

familiar.text: And they reasoned among themselves, saying, It is because we have no bread.

modern.text: So they began to discuss with one another the fact that they had no bread.

original.text: καὶ διελογίζοντο πρὸς ⸀ἀλλήλους ὅτι ἄρτους οὐκ ⸀ἔχουσιν.

verses.restored: Knowing this, he said to them, Why are you reasoning because you have no bread? Do you not yet perceive or understand? Have your hearts been hardened?

familiar.text: And when Jesus knew it, he saith unto them, Why reason ye, because ye have no bread? perceive ye not yet, neither understand? have ye your heart yet hardened?

modern.text: Aware of their conversation, Jesus asked them, “Why are you debating about having no bread? Do you still not see or understand? Do you have such hard hearts?

original.text: καὶ ⸀γνοὺς λέγει αὐτοῖς· Τί διαλογίζεσθε ὅτι ἄρτους οὐκ ἔχετε; οὔπω νοεῖτε οὐδὲ συνίετε; ⸀πεπωρωμένην ἔχετε τὴν καρδίαν ὑμῶν;

verses.restored: Having eyes, do you not see? Having ears, do you not hear? And do you not remember?

familiar.text: Having eyes, see ye not? and having ears, hear ye not? and do ye not remember?

modern.text: ‘Having eyes, do you not see? And having ears, do you not hear?’ And do you not remember?

original.text: ὀφθαλμοὺς ἔχοντες οὐ βλέπετε καὶ ὦτα ἔχοντες οὐκ ἀκούετε; καὶ οὐ μνημονεύετε

verses.restored: When I broke the five loaves for the five thousand, how many baskets full of broken pieces did you take up? They said to him, Twelve.

familiar.text: When I brake the five loaves among five thousand, how many baskets full of fragments took ye up? They say unto him, Twelve.

modern.text: When I broke the five loaves for the five thousand, how many basketfuls of broken pieces did you collect?” “Twelve,” they answered.

original.text: ὅτε τοὺς πέντε ἄρτους ἔκλασα εἰς τοὺς πεντακισχιλίους, πόσους κοφίνους ⸂κλασμάτων πλήρεις⸃ ἤρατε; λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Δώδεκα.

verses.restored: And the seven for the four thousand, how many baskets full of broken pieces did you take up? They said, Seven.

familiar.text: And when the seven among four thousand, how many baskets full of fragments took ye up? And they said, Seven.

modern.text: “And when I broke the seven loaves for the four thousand, how many basketfuls of broken pieces did you collect?” “Seven,” they said.

original.text: ὅτε ⸀καὶ τοὺς ἑπτὰ εἰς τοὺς τετρακισχιλίους, πόσων σπυρίδων πληρώματα κλασμάτων ἤρατε; ⸂καὶ λέγουσιν αὐτῷ⸃· Ἑπτά.

verses.restored: He said to them, Do you not yet understand?

familiar.text: And he said unto them, How is it that ye do not understand?

modern.text: Then He asked them, “Do you still not understand?” The Blind Man at Bethsaida

original.text: καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς· ⸀Οὔπω συνίετε;

verses.restored: They came to Bethsaida. They brought to him a blind man and pleaded with him to touch him.

familiar.text: And he cometh to Bethsaida; and they bring a blind man unto him, and besought him to touch him.

modern.text: When they arrived at Bethsaida, some people brought a blind man and begged Jesus to touch him.

original.text: Καὶ ⸀ἔρχονται εἰς Βηθσαϊδάν. καὶ φέρουσιν αὐτῷ τυφλὸν καὶ παρακαλοῦσιν αὐτὸν ἵνα αὐτοῦ ἅψηται.

verses.restored: Taking the blind man by the hand, he brought him outside the village; spitting on his eyes and placing hands on him, he asked, Do you see anything?

familiar.text: And he took the blind man by the hand, and led him out of the town; and when he had spit on his eyes, and put his hands upon him, he asked him if he saw ought.

modern.text: So He took the blind man by the hand and led him out of the village. Then He spit on the man’s eyes and placed His hands on him. “Can you see anything?” He asked.

original.text: καὶ ἐπιλαβόμενος τῆς χειρὸς τοῦ τυφλοῦ ⸀ἐξήνεγκεν αὐτὸν ἔξω τῆς κώμης, καὶ πτύσας εἰς τὰ ὄμματα αὐτοῦ, ἐπιθεὶς τὰς χεῖρας αὐτῷ, ἐπηρώτα αὐτόν· Εἴ τι ⸀βλέπεις;

verses.restored: Looking up, he said, I see people, because I see them like trees walking around.

familiar.text: And he looked up, and said, I see men as trees, walking.

modern.text: The man looked up and said, “I can see the people, but they look like trees walking around.”

original.text: καὶ ἀναβλέψας ἔλεγεν· Βλέπω τοὺς ἀνθρώπους ὅτι ὡς δένδρα ὁρῶ περιπατοῦντας.

verses.restored: Then again he placed hands on his eyes, and he looked intently and was restored, and he saw everything clearly.

familiar.text: After that he put his hands again upon his eyes, and made him look up: and he was restored, and saw every man clearly.

modern.text: Once again Jesus placed His hands on the man’s eyes, and when he opened them his sight was restored, and he could see everything clearly.

original.text: εἶτα πάλιν ⸀ἐπέθηκεν τὰς χεῖρας ἐπὶ τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτοῦ, καὶ ⸂διέβλεψεν καὶ ἀπεκατέστη καὶ ἐνέβλεπεν⸃ τηλαυγῶς ⸀ἅπαντα.

verses.restored: He sent him away to his house, saying, Do not even enter the village.

familiar.text: And he sent him away to his house, saying, Neither go into the town, nor tell it to any in the town.

modern.text: Jesus sent him home and said, “Do not go back into the village.” Peter’s Confession of Christ (Matthew 16:13–20; Luke 9:18–20; John 6:67–71)

original.text: καὶ ἀπέστειλεν αὐτὸν ⸀εἰς οἶκον αὐτοῦ λέγων· Μηδὲ εἰς τὴν κώμην ⸀εἰσέλθῃς.

verses.restored: Jesus and his disciples went out to the villages of Caesarea Philippi. On the way he questioned his disciples, saying, Who do people say I am?

familiar.text: And Jesus went out, and his disciples, into the towns of Caesarea Philippi: and by the way he asked his disciples, saying unto them, Whom do men say that I am?

modern.text: Then Jesus and His disciples went on to the villages around Caesarea Philippi. On the way, He questioned His disciples: “Who do people say I am?”

original.text: Καὶ ἐξῆλθεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ εἰς τὰς κώμας Καισαρείας τῆς Φιλίππου· καὶ ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ ἐπηρώτα τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ λέγων αὐτοῖς· Τίνα με λέγουσιν οἱ ἄνθρωποι εἶναι;

verses.restored: They said to him, John the Baptist; others, Elijah; others, one of the prophets.

familiar.text: And they answered, John the Baptist: but some say, Elias; and others, One of the prophets.

modern.text: They replied, “Some say John the Baptist; others say Elijah; and still others, one of the prophets.”

original.text: οἱ δὲ ⸂εἶπαν αὐτῷ λέγοντες⸃ ⸀ὅτι Ἰωάννην τὸν βαπτιστήν, καὶ ἄλλοι Ἠλίαν, ἄλλοι δὲ ⸂ὅτι εἷς⸃ τῶν προφητῶν.

verses.restored: He questioned them, But you, who do you say I am? Peter answered him, You are the Messiah.

familiar.text: And he saith unto them, But whom say ye that I am? And Peter answereth and saith unto him, Thou art the Christ.

modern.text: “But what about you?” Jesus asked. “Who do you say I am?” Peter answered, “You are the Christ.”

original.text: καὶ αὐτὸς ⸂ἐπηρώτα αὐτούς⸃· Ὑμεῖς δὲ τίνα με λέγετε εἶναι; ⸀ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Πέτρος λέγει αὐτῷ· Σὺ εἶ ὁ χριστός.

verses.restored: He strictly warned them that they should tell no one about him.

familiar.text: And he charged them that they should tell no man of him.

modern.text: And Jesus warned them not to tell anyone about Him. Christ’s Passion Foretold (Matthew 16:21–23; Luke 9:21–22)

original.text: καὶ ἐπετίμησεν αὐτοῖς ἵνα μηδενὶ λέγωσιν περὶ αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: He began to teach them that it is necessary for the Son of Humanity to suffer many things, be rejected by the elders, chief priests, and scribes, be killed, and after three days rise.

familiar.text: And he began to teach them, that the Son of man must suffer many things, and be rejected of the elders, and of the chief priests, and scribes, and be killed, and after three days rise again.

modern.text: Then He began to teach them that the Son of Man must suffer many things and be rejected by the elders, chief priests, and scribes, and that He must be killed and after three days rise again.

original.text: Καὶ ἤρξατο διδάσκειν αὐτοὺς ὅτι δεῖ τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ ἀνθρώπου πολλὰ παθεῖν καὶ ἀποδοκιμασθῆναι ⸀ὑπὸ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων καὶ τῶν ἀρχιερέων καὶ τῶν γραμματέων καὶ ἀποκτανθῆναι καὶ μετὰ τρεῖς ἡμέρας ἀναστῆναι·

verses.restored: He was speaking the word plainly. Peter took him aside and began to rebuke him.

familiar.text: And he spake that saying openly. And Peter took him, and began to rebuke him.

modern.text: He spoke this message quite frankly, and Peter took Him aside and began to rebuke Him.

original.text: καὶ παρρησίᾳ τὸν λόγον ἐλάλει. καὶ προσλαβόμενος ⸂ὁ Πέτρος αὐτὸν⸃ ἤρξατο ἐπιτιμᾶν αὐτῷ.

verses.restored: Turning and seeing his disciples, he rebuked Peter and said, Go behind me, adversary, because you are not thinking the things of the Divine but the things of humans.

familiar.text: But when he had turned about and looked on his disciples, he rebuked Peter, saying, Get thee behind me, Satan: for thou savourest not the things that be of God, but the things that be of men.

modern.text: But Jesus, turning and looking at His disciples, rebuked Peter and said, “Get behind Me, Satan! For you do not have in mind the things of God, but the things of men.” Take Up Your Cross (Matthew 16:24–28; Luke 9:23–27)

original.text: ὁ δὲ ἐπιστραφεὶς καὶ ἰδὼν τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ ἐπετίμησεν ⸀Πέτρῳ ⸂καὶ λέγει⸃· Ὕπαγε ὀπίσω μου, Σατανᾶ, ὅτι οὐ φρονεῖς τὰ τοῦ θεοῦ ἀλλὰ τὰ τῶν ἀνθρώπων.

verses.restored: Calling the crowd with his disciples, he said to them, If anyone wants to come after me, let that one deny self, take up the cross, and follow me.

familiar.text: And when he had called the people unto him with his disciples also, he said unto them, Whosoever will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me.

modern.text: Then Jesus called the crowd to Him along with His disciples, and He told them, “If anyone wants to come after Me, he must deny himself and take up his cross and follow Me.

original.text: Καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος τὸν ὄχλον σὺν τοῖς μαθηταῖς αὐτοῦ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· ⸂Εἴ τις⸃ θέλει ὀπίσω μου ⸀ἐλθεῖν, ἀπαρνησάσθω ἑαυτὸν καὶ ἀράτω τὸν σταυρὸν αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀκολουθείτω μοι.

verses.restored: For whoever wants to save his life/soul will lose it, but whoever loses his life/soul because of me and the good message will save it.

familiar.text: For whosoever will save his life shall lose it; but whosoever shall lose his life for my sake and the gospel’s, the same shall save it.

modern.text: For whoever wants to save his life will lose it, but whoever loses his life for My sake and for the gospel will save it.

original.text: ὃς γὰρ ⸀ἐὰν θέλῃ τὴν ⸂ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ⸃ σῶσαι ἀπολέσει αὐτήν· ὃς δʼ ἂν ⸀ἀπολέσει τὴν ⸄ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ⸅ ἕνεκεν ἐμοῦ καὶ τοῦ εὐαγγελίου ⸀σώσει αὐτήν.

verses.restored: For what does it profit a person to gain the whole world and forfeit one's life/soul?

familiar.text: For what shall it profit a man, if he shall gain the whole world, and lose his own soul?

modern.text: What does it profit a man to gain the whole world, yet forfeit his soul?

original.text: τί γὰρ ⸀ὠφελεῖ ⸀ἄνθρωπον ⸂κερδῆσαι τὸν κόσμον ὅλον καὶ ζημιωθῆναι⸃ τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ;

verses.restored: For what can a person give in exchange for one's life/soul?

familiar.text: Or what shall a man give in exchange for his soul?

modern.text: Or what can a man give in exchange for his soul?

original.text: ⸂τί γὰρ⸃ ⸀δοῖ ἄνθρωπος ἀντάλλαγμα τῆς ψυχῆς αὐτοῦ;

verses.restored: Whoever is ashamed of me and my words in this adulterous and misaligned generation, of that one the Son of Humanity will also be ashamed when he comes in the glory of his Father with the holy messengers.

familiar.text: Whosoever therefore shall be ashamed of me and of my words in this adulterous and sinful generation; of him also shall the Son of man be ashamed, when he cometh in the glory of his Father with the holy angels.

modern.text: If anyone is ashamed of Me and My words in this adulterous and sinful generation, the Son of Man will also be ashamed of him when He comes in His Father’s glory with the holy angels.”

original.text: ὃς γὰρ ἐὰν ἐπαισχυνθῇ με καὶ τοὺς ἐμοὺς λόγους ἐν τῇ γενεᾷ ταύτῃ τῇ μοιχαλίδι καὶ ἁμαρτωλῷ, καὶ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐπαισχυνθήσεται αὐτὸν ὅταν ἔλθῃ ἐν τῇ δόξῃ τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτοῦ μετὰ τῶν ἀγγέλων τῶν ἁγίων.
